reviewsWithKeywords.title: I don't get the hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We read great things about Playa Delfine so we were excited to go there. We grabbed an Uber, arrived, and... were disappointed AGAIN. This is becoming a pattern on our Mexico trip. The beach has white sand and blue sea, there are restrooms and parasols. But that's the only positive thing I can say about it and that'swhy it gets 2 stars from me. But it's God ugly. The view is atrocious. If you look to the left, there are monstrous hotels. If you look to the right... there are monstrous hotels. It even beats the Belgian coast in ugliness, and the coast from my home country is notorious for having ugly buildings. This was worse, which I didn't even think was possible. But it apparently it is. I refer to the pictures I took from this beach. We were appalled. We did a long beach walk, hoping we would find better parts of the beach, but it only got worse when we reached the hotels. I honestly don't get why on earth people would want to spend their vacation in Cancún when this world has so many alternatives that are so much more beautiful while being so much cheaper. It's not like the atrocious monster hotels that ruin the views are cheap. If they were, I could understand. But they really aren't. On top of that, there was stinking sea weed everywhere. Mass tourism gone wrong in any possible way.This place made me sad.

reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited Los Delfines Beach with my partner and it was a magical experience. We even saw dolphins in the distance, which made the experience even more special.I highly recommend this beach for couples looking for a quiet and cozy spot in Máncora. It's the ideal place to enjoy the sun, the sea breeze, and an unforgettable romantic getaway.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Free Beach with Free Thatch Shade Umbrellas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Free beach. Free parking. Sure, the parking is on the sandy side of the road because the lot is so tiny but it’s all free. What’s more, there are dozens of large thatched umbrellas to sit under (again for free). I saw tons of families on the beach with our family of 5 that included three teens. There is a bathroom but expect to pay the guy for toilet paper. There is also seaweed but much less than Plays Langosta that we visited the next day. Bring your own food and drinks, but I saw several guys walking the beach and selling drinks, fruit, ceviche, etc. The Cancun sign is up in the parking lot which increases traffic. Since the hotels have their beaches basically locked up, this is our #1 choice of Cancun beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A lot of sargassum

But, as you get closer, it shows you the reality: it is full of small sargassum branches, thousands...millions of them. So many that they change the color of the sea, in the surf you can see a very ugly brown color. But if you decide to jump into the sea anyway, be careful, the angle of the slope of the shore is very steep and with a little wave it becomes dangerous. The current pulls very strongly inward.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach, Mirador and the Cancun sign
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On other trips we had seen it from the road and thought it was beautiful, but we never had time to enjoy it. Now we did stay there and it was the one we liked the most of those we were able to visit.It is very wide and as it is located in front of the open sea, it has strong waves.It offers a long strip for parking, but every time we passed it we saw it crowded and this time was no exception.To access the beach itself and the sea you have to walk a fairly steep stretch of sand, so move your little legs! haha.You will find infrastructure to use freely: many palapas, good bathrooms, a large viewpoint and the colorful letters of “CANCUN” for the inevitable photo, (although you must stand in a long line waiting for your turn).The view is beautiful with white sand, turquoise sea and rough waves… we really enjoyed watching the birds, hovering over the sea and diving to catch their food: a postcard that we loved.For those who want to eat something light on the beach, there is a grocery store and a chain sandwich shop less than 1 km away.

Water is soooo much calmer and clearer. P.S. for Playa Caracol, walk down towards the Riu Palace for the perfect less crowded clear water area and good snorkeling off the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I would return many more times, I highly recommend them.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its crystal clear waters and beautiful turquoise blue, it is a true Paradise!!SUPER CLEAN BEACH, A WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent and super equipped public beach with turquoise sea.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to this beach looking for turquoise waters and white sand and it was exactly what we found. Although there was a little sargassum, there were cleaning crews that removed what was left in the sand and kept the beach super clean.This beach has Palapas and some wooden chairs (we arrived at 9:30 am and they were almost all free).We left the car in the parking lot, went down to the beach and enjoyed an incredible day at the beach. There are showers and bathrooms in perfect condition and hygiene to use.From time to time, late in the afternoon, street vendors sell food and drink. We didn't buy anything since we had taken it with us so I can't comment on the prices.Near the parador, in the area of the stones, one could enjoy seeing the iguanas.We were able to enjoy an incredible day at the beach with friends and family.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Los Delfines So Cute
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very nice. To spend a delicious morning. There are some chairs and umbrellas. There are bathrooms to change and you can line up with your drinks and snacks. We visited July 9, 2023 a group of 15 people

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Normal
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The fact that someone waits up to 1 hour for a photo with some letters seems stupid to me.Pro: free bathrooms and showers although with a minimal amount of water.Pro: the viewpoint.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not for little children
reviewsWithKeywords.text: SUPER choppy and strong waters, not great if you have kids under 10 years old. We stayed for 5 minutes before packing up and moving to a different beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: They close the bathroom/showers at 5pm!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was told that this was the only public beach in Cancun. It was nice and clean and we found a palapa. However, they closed the bathrooms and turned off the shower water exactly at 5pm, which was really unfortunate. I went end of April on a Monday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The beach is not for the families with kids.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The place is beatufil but not to enjoy the swiming in the sea with kids. The steep descent into the water. For adults it might be fine. But for the families with kids there are otger places much more suitable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It really is a very beautiful beach, fun and very clean, they have showers and public bathrooms to change and rinse, I have yet to visit more but this was very good.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with easy parking access, local bus system will also drop you off at the main entrance. There are restaurants nearby therefore bring your own amenities. Depending on the currents, wind and waves  the water may not be swimmable, there are only 2 lifeguard stations on the public beach stretch. Amazing views just look at the submitted pictures and plenty of wanna be instagramers/influencers thinking this is their personnel beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I've ever seen. You'll think the pictures are photoshopped until you see it with your own eyes. It is really that beautiful! Water was nice, warm and incredibly blue!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very nice beach, quiet and clean, I liked it very much to be here, everything is very nice and serene, I hope to visit more beaches on this vacation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated and crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I don't have any awesome experience to share. It was crowded and somewhat dirty. Beach at my resort has similar or better views with clean beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Relaxing days enjoying beach and party. A very nice place for vacations  A good service and beautiful accommodation. I will be back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice view of the ocean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited the beach at about 6 in the morning, just in time to watch the sunrise. There was nobody there so the whole place was very quiet and peaceful. The scenery here was just stunning.I know that a lot of people in the comment section complained about the seaweed problem, but compared to where I stayed at (Royalton Riviera) which is further south from the beach, there was a lot less seaweed at the beach the day I was there so I don't think it is a huge problem.Definitely recommend you to go just for the view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, with the Cancun sign to take amazing photos. There are always lines to take pictures, but it’s worth it. There are public restrooms and showers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Scenery But Not Much Else
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Arriving in our taxi, this beach looked gorgeous. Rows of shady palapas free to use and decently kept bathrooms open to all. (In Cancun, nothing is free.)Once we ventured down to the sand, however, it was not very impressive. There were zero services for food or drink. Not even a vendor walking around selling cold drinks from a cooler or anything. Zip.I asked the bathroom attendant where one could get snacks or a beer, and she said go back up to the street level and walk down the street to a convenience store.The seaweed was so thick and the riptide so strong, you can’t really swim either - you just wade in and stand there.  Mountains of seaweed as far down the beach as you can see. I realize there’s not much anyone can do about the seaweed, but nevertheless it does detract from the experience. And like I said, no one was challenging the riptide that I could see, so everyone is packed within about 10 meters of the beach itself.Please note also that certain sections of the bathroom facilities etc. are roped off due to ongoing construction and there is rubble and debris in those areas.There is also one of those ubiquitous photo opp signs in big colorful letters: CANCUN, that everyone takes a photo next to for instagram. It does not matter when you go there, day or night, there is a line of 25 to 50 people waiting to take a photograph next to these letters. I do not understand the allure of this, but anytime we ever drove past this point there was a line down the sidewalk in the hot sun to take a photo next to these letters.Ultimately, we paid $20 for the cab ride to the beach. We each wait it out and got wet in the waves and then sat under the Palapa and dried off. In total we were there less than a half an hour and pretty much got our fill. Then we paid another $20 to go back to our hotel to use the rooftop pool. Pretty scenery but nothing else going for this place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overhyped
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was crowded and Covered in seaweed. So much seaweed it was unpleasant to swim in. It has some limited shade and they don’t offer any chairs or towels to rent like other beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The encounter with the dolphins
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is for lovers of calm, it has a tropical climate where you can enjoy it, it has excellent services. You can relax in the shade of one of the many parasols. When you arrive at Playa de los Delfines you can see that its services are free, there is even a beach for children, I recommend this place because it is amazing how the dolphins are well trained and very beautiful. What makes it really look like an unforgettable experience is its surroundings, since it has a spectacular country ideal for resting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEAUTIFUL BEACH
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a very beautiful beach from the outside that you must visit when you go to Cancun with your family or friends, the color of the sea is incredible contrasting with the white sand, it is a very crowded beach since the Cancun sign is found and everyone comes to drink a beautiful photo. This beach is public and has parking and surveillance, as well as bathroom services and tables to sit and enjoy the view, as well as being quite safe and it is located 20 minutes from downtown Cancun or 10 minutes from the hotel zone. It is a good beach to visit on vacation

reviewsWithKeywords.title: gorgeous ocean view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Five minutes walk from our resort, we went there early in the morning. This beach has a gorgeous ocean view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful and within walking distance or a quick taxi ride from most hotels. It is very touristy, but still gorgeous with the soft sand, clear water and blue skies. Visit this beach and relax if you can.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Way too much seaweed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The view is nice, but however, there is way too much seaweed. People clearly are not trying hard enough to remove the seaweed from the beach. However, they have umbrellas to sit in the shade. Don’t go here during seaweed season, there are many other beaches that are better than this.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ok beach to spend an hour or two
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were told this beach was the best in Cancun, but it's an ok beach, not a great one.People could spend a bit of time here quite happily, but it's definitely not a paradise beachThe beach is ok and the water can be a bit choppy.For far better beaches, head to Mujeres Island, 20mins away by ferry and costing pennies to reach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The mexican Caribbean sea at it's best! Went on a Sunday morning. Lot of waves, clean sand. The water is a bit cold in January. Easy access with R1 bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach I have ever seen, but not for swim
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is by far one of the most beautiful beaches in the world. It is easy to get get there as any bus in Cancun will take you there. It is located in one of the ends of the Kukulkan Blvd. where the access for the beach is located. There are bathrooms available and canopies to give you some shade. Not lots of trees, if any at all to hide from the burning sun. The beach is below under a cliff (access was built - like stairs, however I am not sure if it's modified with wheelchair ramps).Here is the catch: There are a natural reef wall in the shallow part of the beach, right in the area where the wave crashes. It makes it impossible to swim, as the reef wall  natural stone can cut your skin. Also right behind the reef wall the ocean is deep and rough. There are Red flags up along this beach area and coast near by. If you decide to walk along the shore, be aware that the next exit, called Playa Publica (Public Beach) is next to 4 kms walking at the Balenas beach as most of the coast is occupied by private hotel/resorts.  I saw around 3 swimmable spots and it was crowded with people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach to not swim
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go early to enjoy the beach w/ very little people. Beautiful scenery but not calm to swim. You can park there or take the bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach of cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cancun's best beach for sure. One of the few beaches where parking is not a pain and some excellent restaurants nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: INteresting. Local and Tourist Beach Hangout! 150 people out in the water?
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably Cancun's best beach, I imagine. Though I have not visited alot. Large sand area, lots of swimming, police and security presence around to keep watch, and people! Obviously the popular local and mayeb touristy beach spot. If you are looking to swim a little, this is the place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: i like this becuse it is so cool
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this beach is so awesome[  i love this i hope you like it too if you come to this place and if you review it as

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Acces to the beach easy by bus or car. The beach was beautiful but quite crowded for a Friday morning. The waves were quite fierce today ,red flags, no swimming today for me. No restaurants around sobe sure to bring your own stuff.  There are some vendors around that sell some food and drinks. The food is homemade stuff so you are not sure what you are getting. The drinks (beer, margaritas, etc...)usually watered down and cost around 7 dollars. Way too much.Also of note, bathrooms close at 5 pm,  so make sure you go before then

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach. We had a lot of fun. The sand and the sea is beautiful, free outdoor showers are perfect. I love the Cancun sign.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Feedback
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A place to remember! We had an amazing experience, weather was awesome and people so kind. Will be back with my friends next year.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful sight see… and nice place to just chill on the white sand, under the beach stationary umbrellas. The ocean surf is a bit too strong for a swim (my taste), but water is crystal clear. It’s unspoiled by hotels and businesses - very natural feel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very pretty public beach. A little crowded by not rowdy. Very pleasant and no seaweed. Definitely somewhere I'll visit again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach playground
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The kids playground and area near to it was littered with discarded paraphernalia of injecting sort used recreationally and by addicts. That is not good enough. The saving grace is that the water color is appealing to your eyes. Bring in your sunglasses.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Almost excellent but...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would love to give it a 5 because it is truly breathtaking and beautiful. The pictures do not do it justice as far as the turquoise and different shades of blue in the water. The parking is free, which is always good and appreciated, the two biggest issues were the violent surf which makes going in entertaining for a short period of time but not really fun. We could go out maybe 15 yards and that was it before the undertow carried you out to sea. Along with that, the sand, really very very small pebbles, gets in your trunks and embeds itself in your skin, which is very difficult to remove.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach south of Zona Hoteliera
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Delfines is a long and wide stretch of beautiful white powder sand just south from the hotel zone.You won't need to come here if you're staying at one of the hotels by the beach north, as this is the same beach stretching for miles.However, even then I'd recommend doing that to mix up with locals who gather here as this is the public beach and a favorite local spot. On the other hand, for those staying at city ho(s)tels I'd strongly recommend it. You can choose your spot anywhere for free or hire sunbeds and umbrellas for a reasonable fee.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: NICE AND COOL
reviewsWithKeywords.text: perfect for a family picnic there is plenty of space if you want to play with your children or friends you could spend there all day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A wide width, a great view & a lovely sign :)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: At pretty far south along the great stretch of sand for several kilometers right alongside Boulevard Kukulcan running through the Hotel Zone of Cancun (about 9 or 10 kilometers in total, I would say, consisting of beaches with various names) is this part of that great stretch where yes quite likely is "the widest" of all those beaches with one reason being the lack of oceanfront high-rises unlike at the other beaches along the stretch (definitely wider than Playa Chacmool near where I stayed at about 8 kilometers to the north which is an area just cluttered with plenty of high-rises right beside that beach).  And then yes, there are three "enhanced features" of this beach including one on it & two right above: a number of "straw umbrellas", a "viewing deck" for a great panorama of the "deep-blue" sea & wide sky above (where at the time was some long kite flying in the air), and a nice-sized & colorful 'Cancun' sign (for a pretty good photo-op with the sea in the background).  And with no significantly big waves that I could see walking right up to the water's edge, this may be a good beach for a swim (but so it seemed also at Playa Chacmool near my place and only to get pummeled by the waves after entering so that beach not one I would suggest!).And nearby, which is just across Blvd. Kukulcan and a short few-minute walk to the left after coming up from this beach, is the El Rey "ruin site" (with a nice number of structures on a rectangular ground to walk back & forth between its two ends); and not too close to this beach but to get to easily by just taking a short ride of 5 to 10 minutes on a public bus is the big museum Museo Maya de Cancun (with not too many but a fair number of Mayan artifacts and where there's also just adjacent to the museum building is the small site of San Miguelito which is like a mini-forest with a few number of ruin structures).  And also, as for the 'Cancun' sign (as mentioned above), there are also two more of that sign pretty identical to the one above this beach (one which is a "lakeside sign" right beside the big Nichupte Lake on the opposite side of Blvd. Kukulcan and about 6 or 7 kilometers to the north from this beach which is just a little past La Isla Shopping Village; and one at like the "downtown or centro" area of the Hotel Zone which is actually the one I "highly suggest" with also a great outdoor wall mural nearby depicting a "quaint & colorful" scene of the old Cancun or such).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well worth the visit.  Especially if your resort doesn't have a nice beach.  The view is stunning, and the water beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I thought of visiting this beach since it is popular, but it was really crowded. Best to do is to get there early so you don't have a lot of people at the time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect with kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth to visit, we went with kids and they like that sea is very calm. Depends on the wind. Take snacks with you

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beat is absolutely beautiful you won't find many better than this easy to get to so easy to enjoy everyone was friendly and help make my time a wonderful experience

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beatiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a big beach so there is plenty of space for everyone! The waves are usually quite big and that is the only downside. There is a 'Cancun' sign with a nice background for a photo but... the queue to it is usually quite long! It is easily accessible by bus or if you coming by car then there is a car park.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not very crowded considering it's a public beach.  There are fruit stands,  palapas, and rinsing areas. The sand is very clean and I would highly recommend coming here if you don't feel like paying for a beach club. Grab a cooler with some food and snacks!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful public  beach but the tides are high
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I loved the beach, it was clean and so blue. This is where you find the famous Cancun sign that many tourists stop by and take pictures at. It is a public beach. There was a little hut by a Tiki bar that offered a massage. I had the most amazing massage for an hour and only paid $20 tip included. It was a better massage than a 30 min massage at my 5 star hotel which costed me over $400. I recommend this beach, you'll love the pristine blue waters and the pictures you'll take will be immaculate

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Delfines
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Huge beach with parking in front. Crystal blue sea, but to many waves. Pay attention on local people, everyone wants to robber you. There is only one very expensive place where you can buy food and drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely Most Beautiful Beach in Cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most stunning and widest stretch of the beach in Cancun. Ideal for relaxing after a long day of tourism around the city. It's waters are the bluest ever, perfect temperature, and not too wavy. It's white sand goes as far as the eyes can carry, and it's not too hot as usually you would expect in very sunny places. The beach is very clean, and great for all ages. Saw many people doing kite surf, canoeing, and jet skiing. Swimming is perfect and no need to worry about little ones as the water level barely reaches higher than your (adult's) knees. There are safeguards running up and down the beach throughout all day. I couldn't see vendors of water and food, but there were public toilets available - with showers. It's easier to reach this beach by car, but a very convenient bus stop is right on the sidewalk. It's a perfect spot for photos. Take your camera!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Delfines is a nice place to spend the afternoon. The beach is very beautiful and clean. Would definitely go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice spot to take pictures.  Go at a off time to take pictures.  Like really early in the morning.  It has the CANCUN sign to take pictures in front of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sandy beach - What a view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went with the kids, and had a great time. We arrived at around 8am, and it was essentially deserted. There are bathrooms (yes you will pay for tp if you need/want any). The waves were awesome that day, and the beach was super clean and free of any debris. There is a little bit of an undertoe, so be careful if you're not a swimmer, and I certainly wouldn't suggest letting the kids swim without supervision. I know it starts to get busy around 11am, so we took off at about that time, and grabbed a shower to clean off before we jumped back in the car.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Windy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was very windy and the sea was too wavey to swim in. It was 250 pesos to hire sunbeds and an umbrella but unfortunately we got scammed, the guy went off to get us change and sent someone else over giving us the wrong amount of change (he pocketed 50 pesos) so we couldn’t even dispute it as he didn’t understand us. The beach was clean but there are much nicer beaches that are less touristy elsewhere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand and sea - beach, blue waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great place to spend a few hours, especially if you have a few hours to kill before your flight out.  it is located  just 15 minutes by car from the airport and It is used by locals.Sun bed (2) and umbrella can be had for around 250 paso. A bar for drinks is also right here, although no food.This beach is right by the Hotel Zone and enjoys beautiful soft sand beaches and delightful pure blue waters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 31st Birthday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really beautiful sand its white the water is clear that u can see right thru its really awesome i love it never seen a place like this beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Today we were there but it was quite windy. Some people told us it was absolutely beautiful when the water was flat. It's at the end of the hotel zone way at the end and it was worth the trek. There are a few guys back and  forth  selling coconut, fruit and trying to promote the restaurant. Prices for the restaurant were way overpriced. But there's nothing else out there. Palapas for free. You could rent a lounger if you wanted to pay. We would go back it was a lovely day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A dream away from building
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I counted 5 shades of blue of the water from indigo to shades of turquoise and baby blue. Lovely spot with umbrella (250 pesos all day) Quiet compared to other areas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top world beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The contrast of white sand and aqua crystal clear waters, make this place unique!Highly recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Sunrise it’s Just Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful in all the aspects. We arrived early so we decided to go see the sunrise at this beach, let me tell you it will for everything be an amazing memory.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I walked up from the Mayan Museum just so I could get my picture at the Cancun sign. There was not a long wait when I went (about 10 mins but I went about 930am) and everyone waited patiently while others were getting their photo taken. I was a solo traveler and it was not an issue getting someone to take my picture. The area was completely safe and I recommend it if you want to get your photo op at the sign.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there last Saturday and it was a little hard to find a parking spot across the street, so be patient if you're driving. There are public bathrooms. The beach is beautiful and the sea waves are stunning.  The umbrella guys trying to rent you an umbrella are annoying,  but you can put your towels anywhere on the beach without charge, like all the beaches we visited in the Riviera Maya,  even if you're in front of a resort beach. All beaches are public.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Public Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the few public beaches.At my time of visit (November/December2019) not crowded.Only a few local people want to sell drinks and snacks, but they are friendly and not annoying.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The draw here for most visitors is the Cancun sign, but the beach itself is absolutely beautiful and extremely clean. Even though it’s a public beach for locals, it’s right in the middle of the hotel zone, but easy to get to by public transportation. We were there on a weekday but the beach was pretty crowded, so I can only imagine what the crowd might look like on the weekends. Nevertheless, it’s a breathtaking setting not to be missed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Delfines, beautiful and captivating
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in the area of Cancun is Delfines (Dolphins), you might even have the chance to see one if you're lucky. White sand, light blue and light green ocean, plenty of space to enjoy and a perfect spot to have a selfie.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is close to the center of Cancun and I went easily by bus to there. It is clean. I walked there a long precursor to visiting closed areas. It was very calm and cool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have visited several beaches in Quintana Roo and Delfines is my favorite. The waves can hit a bit hard for small children. However, it has an incredible view and good food service! Love, love this beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Never seen a beach like it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Never been on a beach holiday it wasn't my cup tea but i will say that the beach is beautiful it is a must see. Not too busy was lovely we took a stroll along the beach it was hot so defiantly wear a hat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cancun Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is amazing. It is definitely a must see. The beaches are heavenly. The locals can get persistent at times, but I guess that's business.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the view. Theres so much to get into and its really relaxing. Great to take pictures for photo shoots and also a wonderful place to SLEEEEEEEP

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful and clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Thia vbeach is relaly beautiful and very clean. Its a very good place for family outing . Especially in the evening

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I think the best part of Playa Delfines is that there are free umbrellas to use. And like any other beach access int he hotel zone it has showers, toilets, and rental of beach chairs, drinks, and food. Make sure to bring your own soft drinks and water since the drinks available are mostly cocktails and beer. I went there several times since I lived in Cancun, and it is the best beach to go for a swim

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but with plenty of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is really beautiful, but with a lot of people on it. We came from Oleo hotel, by bus, and had a crazy experience with a stupid driver of R2 27. This guy drove like crazy whike speaking of the phone or searching for music on the phone, so we enjoyed even more to arrive on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic Beach, Beautiful White Sand!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have visited this gorgeous beach on the way to Cancun and really loved it, the water was so clean and blue, sand was so nice and there where only few people on the beach. Be careful of the high surf break, some of the waves looked very strong. Would love to come back there next time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: love it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: if you are running out of beach time in your hotel, this is the beach to stay. Bars are quiet expensive therefore a beer or soda can hit 2,50 dollars. However you do have a beach bed or table and umbrella....of course it depends on the time you arrive to find place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Welcome to Cancun!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful place to see the sea. Yeah the big sign is there, but that's nothing compared to the view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can't relax
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic clean white sand beach but you can't relax because you bombarded by vendors and waiters who are selling stuffs like cold-drinks, palapas, towels, soda, food, etc and feel irritated.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An iconic beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Playa Delfines seems to be located dead in the centre of the spit upon which the almost 'over the top' Zona Hotelera has been constructed. There is also an iconic sign at which so many visitors take their souvenir snapshots. We gave that one a miss, though, and instead concentrated upon the lovely turquoise waters and soft white sands..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful part of cancun If you have the time go and visit Coastline there is lovely and peaceful. Well worth it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic clean white sand beach with very little seaweed present when I visited.  Didn't use them but there were toilet & shower facilities available.  Public bus stop at one of the main entrances to the beach which run to & from Cancun Centro.  I think the cost was 12 peso one way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I don't understand the buzz...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perhaps I came in with expectations that were too high, but this beach was described as a 'must-see' on this and many other review sites. The biggest and best in Cancun. We came in as a family of four hoping for a perfect beach day but we left this beach after about two hours. Yes, the beach is massive, the sand is nice like most Yucatan beaches and there are so many places to sit. But we were constantly bombarded by vendadores and waiters selling us coco-drinks, tables, palapas, towels, soda, food, etc. that it was never very comfortable or relaxing. There was some sargassum on the shores and shallow areas although overall the water was still nice and beach was walkable. Snorkeling and swimming were out of the question due to the high and turbulent surf. We did have fun jumping in the waves and were surprised at how far the shallow water extends. This is the beach with the colorful 'Cancun' selfie sign, so there are ALWAYS cars and people in the single row parking lot. They usually have attendants at the street side lot helping to guide you in - of course expecting compensation for their efforts. I just don't understand the 4.5 star rating for this beach. It wasn't nearly as nice as other public beaches. The beach in front of our hotel was so much better than Playa Delfines. If you don't have a hotel beach, there are many, many better public beach options nearby. One note: access to the beach is provided by a very steep stairway.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Local Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Delfines was simply amazing. We rented chairs with umbrellas for about $16 per person for 6 hours. They have a restaurant/bar on the beach which was perfect. The food was so tasty and affordable. I would definitely recommend taking the bus from your hotel (only $1) and hitting up this local beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The beach looks gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Also here is the famous view in which you will find the "CANCUN" letter sign. I recommend bringing a cool drink if you are planning on staying there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice colors, what a pity with this seaweed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very beautiful, a good place for surfing and swimming. What a pity with this seaweed.... the beach it’s very accessible with public bus (R1/R2) cost 12 pesos one way. You can stop the bus everywhere. Take your beverages, or you can order something (cocktails with alcool 150 pesos, without 120 pesos). The mexican authorities are trying to clean this beach, but the waves are powerful and a lot algas are dropped to the seashore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent the better part of the day hanging out on this beach, it was cool.  The water is rough in this area but really beautiful.  There was quite a bit of seaweed the day we went but it was still really nice.  We rented a umbrella and chairs & also purchased some adult beverages right on the beach at a really affordable price.  As a bonus we snapped a few pics with the Cancun sign before we left.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Cancun selfie sign
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the place for the selfie.Few iguanas to grab a picture.Beach was clean when we turned up, it was early morning to void waiting in the heat.Took a bus for a dollar each way from the main hotel zone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's an aesthetically pleasing beach with the nice colourful Cancun sign. When we visited the beach there were loads of people lined up to take a pic by it but on passing around 6am, it was basically empty. It is accessible by public transport but we had a rental car. There was a person in the car park who was aggressively demanding a tip and even waited for us when we were leaving. When arriving on the beach, multiple persons tried to sell us various items. We eventually purchased food and drink and some beach chairs. The water was rough, high waves and there was a dip in the sea floor (at least at the location that I was at). There was a lot of sargassum on the shoreline as well as floating in the water. The amazing thing was the toilets. The free toilets are located at three places across the beach, there are maps on the beach that can identify them. Yeh attendant was VERY pleasant and ensured everyone had much of a clean experience as possible.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: O.k . amenities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful, IF YOU HAVE A CAR- we are staying in Cancun centro and were dropped of by our taxi there, thank god the taxi driver told me that it was very difficult to get a return taxi (& it was true I tried getting a return taxi w my app and it did not work), so keep that in mind. We arranged a ride back how ever from Cancun centro to the beach it was only $212 pesos but to come back it was $600. The beach is not worth all that to me.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach with little seaweed!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After being crushed because of the seaweed situation here we found this beach.  Close to the Cancun sign its clean. The seaweed is control and not much in the water.  We were greeted by a beach vendor that got us 2 beach chairs and an umbrella. He came with a menu for drinks and food throughout the day. Very relaxing.  Free food vendors walking around with local treats like fruit and shrimp cocktails. A few guys treated us with music for a tip. ( Spanish rap) my kids stayed in the water for hours and were not ready to go. They even saw iguanas which are the norm in this area. Good spot worth visiting if you want crystal water without the fuss.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Local's beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: At the beginning of the hotel zone. We'd been many years ago, but this time it seemed to be really busy most days. A bit of seaweed right now but a beautiful beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a welcome to cancun.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You really know you're in Cancun when you hit the big cancun sign. People are lined up to have their picture taken with the cancun SAM. But what's really the attraction is the beach in the city itself. Absolutely stunning

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach, we stayed in a hotel about 20 min from here! We took public transportation to the beaches. This one has the colorful Cancun sign. Make sure you wear sunscreen, sunglasses & hat there is a long line. Oh & water bottle. You can seat on a covered umbrella for 20 pesos. We ordered a hamburger meal. The hamburger was the best I've tried not exaggerating! You can order coconut water. Once your done with the water they come & pick it up chop the coconut up for you add lime and hot sauce for you to eat. All while you just sitting at the beautiful beach like a queen 😂

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beautiful beach nice and clean and clear sand. Nice friendly locals so friendly and sea water was warm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Got there early to get a free palapa - thought we wouldn't need sunscreen if we stayed in the shade - ouch! Use it! Easy free parking!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach....love and towel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing views and sunny days...great se and sand for free parking or depens1 your hotel location you can walk nice pictures

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most popular beaches in Cancun.The view is amazing but the beach wasn't like the pictures I have seen, there was seaweed but not too much, the color of the water is crystal blue however it was too windy so we couldn't swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: PERFECT WAVES and tranquility!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We use to live in Cancun back in the 90s and this beach was our HANG OUT! Its better now since they added bath rooms and palapas! Its beautiful and we go back every year! Please check it out if you are a BEACH DWELLER!! Its one of the best beaches in the world!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEAUTIFUL OMG
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I must say this beach is so damn beautiful. wow. so clean so scenic and epic that I took 2 hours just enjoying the moment. the huts that line the beach made it feel so tropical and exotic. very close to hotels and public buses going to and from this beauty. lots of police walking around making you feel safe. one thing I would say is to walk with your own food and drinks. Very windy and the water was very choppy and strong currents so be aware. Could just been the time of the year. but I must say enjoy this beach as much as I did and Thank me later.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beauriful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A really lovely beach with excellent amenities nearby. Free,  toilets 5 pesos, and many shops. Notably surfing coconut

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach very close to our hotel. Water was very choppy today but beautiful anyway. Police around so felt very safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great public beach but bring your own food
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I like this beach very accessible to public bus using R1/R2 going in and out of hotel zone. You have to bring your own food though because there are no restaurants nearby or food trucks. There’s a Cancun sign there that always have long lines so be there early.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Canton!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We just returned from our Anniversary trip to Cancun. We had an Amazing time! Stayed at the Royal Solaris (7 nights) and Panama Jack's ( for one night). We felt VERY safe everywhere we visited, walked and rode the public bus. The beaches had little Sargassum when we arrived, but 4 days in we could see huge patches of it in the water coming in, which made pretty large piles in the sand. All the beach along the Hotel zone was the same. Our week was fantastic! We did swim in the ocean but it was super windy the entire time which made the waves larger than normal and lots of areas with riptides. We are already planning our next trip later this year, after visiting Los Cabos!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: top #4
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are tired of the standard beaches along the Hotel Zone, visit Playa Delfines, a beautiful and very large beach with fine sand and slightly intense waves located near El Rey archaeological zone. Here, you can rent chairs and beach umbrellas as well as bring your own drinks and snacks. You will also find bathrooms, showers, "palapas" and parking lot, all these services totally free. Here you will also find a beautiful wooden lookout with the colorful "Cancún" sign that appears on many of the city´s postcards and brochures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Seriously lovely public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our AirBnB host recommended Delfines to us - and we visited twice. Jaw dropping ocean colors. We found parking with ease (tipped $4 US). The beach is clean as people care for it and pick up after themselves. We brought our own sun cover, but they are available for rent. Bring pesos on the weekend to buy beach food from fresh fruit to fried items. A big drink is $150 plus tip (come on they are running in the hot sun!) Waves crash right at the shoreline so it can be 'fun' getting in and out of the water, but it is so lovely to wave hop. Great people watching, felt safe as there were so many families. $10 pesos if you need to use facilities. Colors are just amazing and you are away from the hotel zone.  We loved it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really enjoy Cancun, day trip , beach, day trip, beach...and I would do again worm water, white sand, turquoise seaGo for it, I am not even beach boy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice public beach (playa)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long and nice public playa, reachable via public buses from any place in Cancun, possible servis if you want (drink, food), not annoying people, "coconut" umbrella for free.Sea not peaceful therefore not ideal for swimming but waves great enough to enjoy for hours. ;-)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As an American in Cancun for an all-inclusive vacation, I'd wondered about this public beach. This trip, I walked down the sand to this beach. It's suprising to me both the size and available amenities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best local open beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the local open beaches along the city coast within the hotel zone. The public is welcome to take an ice chest with any beverages as long as they are cans. Safe & secure. Also open to the public 24/7. There is a beach lounge chair & umbrella service available for free as long a you buy drinks from them. Only a few options, about $8/1 liter cocktail.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: dolphins were great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dolphin Discovery was a great experience. used our resort credit from Moon Palace. when we arrived at dolphin discovery they first offered an upgrade to 2 dolphins for $30 usd per person. then we swam with tbe one dolphin. it was very well organized. dolphins were amazing. woyldnt let you take your own pictures tho. their pictures were $40 per person per picture. or $240 for like 20 pictures. they WERE great photos, but we just couldnt add tbat cist after spending $220 already. :( i do wish we had a couple photos. but the experience was great.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the stop!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the largest of the public beaches in Cancun's Hotel Zone. The parking area/entrance is elevated above the beach itself so the views are amazing! They also have the giant mulit-colored "CANCUN" sign here but be prepared to wait in line as it's the most popular.They have showers and baths, free palapas for shade, handicap accessible and plenty of room. There are not many options for food or drink near this beach. There is usually one small bar/restaurant open down on the beach, just look for the shaded hut. You fill find locals selling water and fruit but don't expect a large selection of places offering food and drink. Best to go prepared with water and snacks. They also offer chairs and umbrellas for rent if you prefer a more comfortable setup.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The view was incredible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was my first time in Cancun and I went with my family. We have fun in the Playa Delfines, the view was incredible and we take a lot of photos on the big letters of Cancun!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Cancún beach !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice blue water, spacious, not much overcrowded, quiet enough to have siesta in the shadow. Just the only restaurant-bar is a bit pricy. Easy excess by a bus from Zona Hoteliera, free of charge umbrella if you are lucky enough to reserve on time, save enough with police passing by time to time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the world’s most beautiful beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cancun certainly has some of the world’sMost beautiful beaches with its white sand and brilliant water colors!Playa Delfines is Cancun at its most picturesque. It’s worth a special trip to see it if you’re anywhere else n the area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great public beach with parking, bathrooms and shade. Minimal parking available. Great views. Soft sand. Lookout point and picture opportunity. Large CANCUN sign for pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great day at the beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a great day at Playa Delfines this week. The parking is along the street and the attendants work for tips. There was a lot of room on the beach and it was very clean. There are a lot of waiters along the beach, but they are very respectful if you don't order. We did order some tacos and guacamole. Delicious!Also, the waves are rough, but we were able to play in the surf a bit. We would go back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Sandy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I stayed at Club Presidente because I felt I needed to be by the strip.  Don't get me wrong it was beautiful. However was able to experience a all inclusive hotelthey had everything you could imagine 5 pools, games, nightclub, casino, theatre plus more. You don't pay for anything, no hassle carrying cash no where or risks of getting robbed. Everything in located and included in ur stay even your transportation to and from airport.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just for the view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visit this beach only for the Cancún sign and that is about it. The waves and sea life at this location makes it dangerous to go for a swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach I have ever been to
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Before vising Cancun, I searched for best beach for family and most people recommended this beach. When I reached the beach, I was awestruck with the beauty of this beach. Crystal clear turquoise blue water with just the perfect waves...The water was not cold so you can enjoy playing in the beach as much as you want.. It also has good showers and washrooms which you can used by paying very minimum feed of 5 pesos; I am sure you will tip more than that :-)  It also has a kind of observatory deck where you can take photos to make your friends jealous :-) If you go to Cancun, don't miss this beach. Happy traveling

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White sand and turquoise crystal water is what you’ll find in all the Mexican Caribbean coast. Sometimes you can even surf a little. The beach itself is gorgeous, and if staying at a 5 star hotel, it’s paradise!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise for free
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful location in Cancun and best of all for free! Just bring your towel and sunscreen and you’re all set! With big hotels and resorts nearby you can see a diverse crowd, and swim in the turquoise blue sea. Free chairs are provided with a valid ID.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach and vieuw. But very wavy and undertow so cant go into ocean too far.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quite busy and big line up in front of Cancun sign !Need to go down hill to get to beach and climb back up to leave.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great looking beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We didn't go into the waters but the view of the beach was lovely!      The beach itself was a bit crowded

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach in Cancun.  The Cancun sign is no longer there to take a photo by.  The sign corroded away. Really nice beach.  Military police presence there which while it made me safe, makes me think why they need to be there. There were some sketchy people around. Probably safe during the day but not at night.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must do in Cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice public beach where you can hang out and enjoy the waves and sun By the way, waves were strong when I was there so don't go too far into the sea

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach and ocean...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach and ocean. If you are lucky, it’s not windy. It’s like Virginia Beach or Myrtle Beach but 12 months. Drink, party and have fun...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxation in a piece of blue heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Classic beautiful beach in Cancun located at a great spot. I would say you can bring your family there or at least it had a friendly ambience during my visit. The view was beautiful and allowed me to take a lot of nice photographs

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa delphin beach cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. But watch out for these guys. There posted on beach selling jet ski rides. We bought a hour then they shortened it to 30min. Trying to get is to pay more money after 30min. Total rip off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't bother
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was highly recommended but it appeared to be a disappointment. Everyone wanted to sell us something (which of course is nothing new in Cancun) and the sand was full of sharp stones all over the place. Sure, the water is beautiful here but so it is everywhere else in the whole beach along the hotel zone. No need to come here again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best views in town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the best place to take a nice picture from your trip to Cancun, here you will be able to see all colors related to the Caribbean, and that special turquoise Cancun color

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best free activity to those who do not stay in hotel zone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A rare nice thing local government provides to those who do not stay in hotel zone. You can still enjoy the same beautiful beach without staying in most expensive resort in town. Shower, changing rooms also provided. Limited parking and prepare to wait in a line if you want to take a picture of  the sign “Cancún”. No wait, no line in early morning . This will be equivalent to people waiting in line for similar picture in Key West, FL "Southernmost" sign.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean and nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It looks like it is one of the nicest beaches in Cancun. Many locals you can also meet here.Waves were really high at the time we  visited it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went to this beach because everyone said it was a must.  It is a beatiful beach.  It is also really large, which is not the case with many other beaches,  I spent a few hours there and do recommend it.Two downsides - 1) The beach drops off where the water comes in.  Just be aware, because I saw many people fall over, not realizing there was a steep drop off.  2) the water is really rough!  I am an experienced ocean swimmer and a surfer and I found the water difficult.  The waves come in fast, right on top of each other, and it is difficult to get out far enough to not be knocked over.  Make sure you have a swimming partner!Sea weed - this is a problem all over Mexico.  They are making a huge effort to curb it's impact.  Each beach has several men raking up leaves and heavy loader trucks to cart the seaweed away, so it is manageable for tourists, but it is there and does create a foul odor.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful public beach in the cancun hotel zone. A easy bus trip from your hotel. and only costs 1 USD to get there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: the place to be
reviewsWithKeywords.text: very nice, big and well organised beach. bring your own food and drinks cause there's OXO around. Toilets and shower available and free

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach with huge waves.A couple of places on the beach to eat.Just check the price of drinks as we were  charged the same price for a virgin pina colada as an alcoholic one as it was expensive.The eating place allowed you to use a sunbed for free if buying drinks etc.I believe this may be the protected beach that the turtles lay their eggs.Saw a number of large iguanas here.There are public toilets and a small shower available.If you walk this beach you cannot get off until you reach another public beach as a number of hotels are on this beach and you are not allowed access.The Cancun sign is also here but you will need to queue for a photo.Worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Parking by donation, nice area, beautiful beach, salesmen offer refreshments or you can bring your own lunch and enjoy there,  popular tourist beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blue, blue Cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All the beaches in Cancun are public, but because of the huge hotels and beachfront development you can't get access to it! The government has remedy this by making 7 entrances to the beaches.  Playa Delfines is one of the best ones!  Great wave action, wide sandy white beach,  bathroom facilities.   Everyone goes here to take a picture with the Cancun colorful sign.  Very popular, limited parking and  congested on the weekends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was very clean and well kept . However there was not much activities on site and you could not easily get food or drinks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a cute public beach.It also has the cancun sign for your pictures.You can bring your own food and enjoy a day in the sand

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean, White sand, Blue water, beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is quite clean and beautiful. The small shades are available. It is by the Cancun Sign board. I did not see a lot of crowd during the thanks giving weekend I was visiting the city. It is one of the must go places if you are visiting Cancun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cancun Sign
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the things I’ve always wanted to visit but was always too far away from it to make a quick stop but this time round I managed to do it me and my fiancé walked from Crown Paradise Club Cancun which took 5 mins to get there and we got there at sunrise and it was unbelievable sunrise with the Cancun sign in front we got there before any crowds gathered and had lot of time for photo opportunity although we enjoyed the sunrise while sitting on the sign we recommend it to everyone but make sure your early we did speak to a couple that waited over an hour just for a picture and were being charged for some guy to take pictures with there own camera so do be beware of this early is better

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice clean beach beyond the hotel area with public access for free, still you need to pay a parking fee. Includes showers and restrooms as well as sunbeds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Seaweed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This used to be one of the most beautiful beaches in Quintana Roo, however, the seaweed thing makes the beach look bad, the water is almost brown and there is seaweed in and out the sea so you can swim properly either, my suggestion check the news about this before to visit it so you can pick a different beach up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Especially good in low season
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has a ‘cancun’ sign so lines are up. Even in the low season. But If you walk a little bit further you’ll find small beach bars with fresh nacho’s, cocktails and beers. Loved the white sand and the abandoned crashed down hotel and the iguana’s.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach the views are beautiful the water is incredible. You should stay there for hours. A must see

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a must see place, the beaches are clean and there are places to take a shower as well as bathrooms

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent white sand shallow beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fabulous shallow water for the longest time, very clean safe beach, go to local store to pick up a lunch and drinks, several available along the road across the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to be
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a really beautiful beach, it has an amazing view and it is so relaxing to be here me and my boyfriend loved this beach !!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cancun beach from London
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What an amazing place this location is - one of the best beaches I have been to.It's a family venue and always a pleasure to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Watch your weather
reviewsWithKeywords.text: On most days, this is one of the prettiest beaches in the world.  Clear water, waves to play in, and beach service from the little palapa restaurant.  Most swimmers are Mexican families who take the bus or drive up from Cancun City, which gives the beach a different vibe than the big hotels that flank it.  There are some shelters for the early arrivers, but if it is busy, you'll want to bring an umbrella or rent one -- the sand may be cool but the sun is HOT! Also had issues on one visit with seaweed near the beach that made it less fun to swim.When you arrive, make sure to get a menu and the notice of the beach restaurant, and they will be happy to bring you food and drinks all day long! And don't miss the individual food vendors -- the mango and watermelon are great in the heat, and I loved the fried cheese.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BAD WEATHER
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately, the beach was full of seaweeds. Red and Yellow flags for 5 days. It was impossible to even touch the water. Something unusual in Cancun for this month of August. Beaches usually are crystal clear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best View in Cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wide open public beach, gorgeous views, turquoise color water and white sand. Limited parking, worth the efford!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Caution
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful Beach, but a little bit dangerous if you aren’t a great swimmer. Lots of algea cloud the clean water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Given the massive amounts of Sargassum we have been having in Quintana Roo, we have been visiting local beaches with hopefully less seaweed. To our delight, Playa Delfines is such a beach. Did it have some the day we visited, yes but the water was awesome. The current and waves seemed to carry it quickly away so it didn’t impact our level of enjoyment. Of course the view from the road was specular.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice beach for a "Kodak moments capture"
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa delfines is a nice beach where you can click very nice photos. I would refer you to visit this beach in start evening time (when you have more light) as you can have very nice shots here. This beach also has a CANCUN capitals for enhanced photo experience. This beach also has some attractive bench and chair options. Also you can find a lot of small SPA and message people (in tents) which can make you relax. For me it was relaxing and I spent a very good time here. Hope you also enjoy!!!

Lovely beach. Although lucky lucky men can be quite pushy but that’s expected anywhere you go abroad.  Lots of sun beds, well there was for the hotel I was staying at anyway, often waiters will come onto the beach for you if you look after them. Sand is lovely and generally clean with barely any litter. Activities to do on the beach, parasailing, jet skis etc.ConsCan often be a lot of seaweed at the start of the sea which can be annoying

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Playa Delfines when my wife and I had stopped to get photo with Cancún sign, we went early in morning around 9:30/10am and with only a few people in front of us we avoided long queues, in mid afternoon can get very busy. The beach itself is stunning, the water is turquoise blue, we found it great especially for photos. Def recommend 👍

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped by this beach on our way out of Cancun. It took forever to get there due to some road work going on but it was worth seeing the gorgeous emerald green water. This water and sand at this beach is magical and almost unbelievable that it’s real.  We didn’t swim but I’d recommend going early as there is hardly any shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Public Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great, well maintained public beach. We stayed at a nearby resort and visited after a trip to the El Rey ruins. Lots of iguanas to feed, locals selling fruits and drinks, and of course the famous Cancun sign. We didn't take a photo with the sign because the sun was hot and the line was very long, but we enjoyed the beach just the same! We took some nice photos by the water, and also got to watch pelicans dive for fish. I would definitely go back to the beach if I am ever in Cancun again!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, good prices.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is nice, there are “palapas” available but you have to get there early to get one, otherwise you can rent an umbrella, two chairs and a table for $200 pesos. Lately there is a seaweed problem so sadly it dampens the experience but the sand is still amazing and we took a nap feeling the amazing breeze and being lulled by the sound of the ocean.There’s people there that offer food, refreshments and they work hard to keep the beach clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful public beach for walking, swimming, sand castles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most popular beach in Cancún is within walking distance of many beach hotels.  It’s popular with tourists and locals alike.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sight
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped to see the beautiful beach and got an adventure that we hope no one else has to experience!  The view was something else! The beach has some rocky areas and the waves were rougher than average ocean.  We dropped our bags under an unbrella and went to take pictures. We made the mistake of leaving our stuff unattended! It only took a minute! Use precautions and keep our stuff with you!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The colors at the site are unique, services like restrooms anda showers are available. Buses and parking area. One of the iconic beaches in Cancún and is very clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: the best public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: one of the must amazing public Beach's of cancun ... you dont need any tour or turistic guide .. just take a bus and say that you go playa delfines they gonna stop there !  the best our is between 6 - 9  early morning!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Water & Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had family photos taken here by Jorge Rodriguez Photography.  Besides the beautiful water & beach, there is a large, brightly colored "CANCUN" sign at the top that makes a wonderful backdrop!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was beautiful and clean, but it is difficult to climb back up to where the bathrooms are or where you parked the car

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I did not find it best for swim but yeah great beach with thatched umbrellas.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have read on the blog, the further south you go, more turquoise water you 'll see. It’s true. You get here by any R1 bus, the Cancun sign will welcome you, but you have to be in the line sometimes.Note:  you can also see Cancun sign at Playa Langosta beach and it has the better background like a palm tree in the back.Coming to Beach, it has a wide area with the thatched umbrella. I would recommend coming early to get one of these if you 'll come after 11-12 in the noon, you won’t find even space to sit there, it is that crowded.Delfines beach and beach south to this are not recommended for swimming as water can be harsh, aggressive some time but it’s not that bad even if you compare to USA East coast beaches. Beautiful turquoise warm water, soft sand, and sun make it amazing. A bathroom is available here unlike other beaches.Cancun’s north beaches are more known for swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach, it has really gotten a bit too Touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Still just as beautiful as ever.  Great fresh fruit and coconut being sold for very cheap.  A bit of hassling at the beach trying to get you to go here or there (Vendors).  Overall a good experience.  It's ridiculous the line to take a picture with the Cancun sign!  The buses will pick you up right there which is handy, although we waited 15 minutes before the bus left waiting for more passengers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best public beaches in Zona Hotelera
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Huge waves because it's not covered by Isla Mujeres but less seaweeds compared to 1-9 km. Rather wide, enough people to not feel abandoned and not crowded at the same time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Delfines
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Delfines Beach (Kilometer 17.7) Getting There By Bus: Blue Line Stop #20, Green Line Stop #17 This one is hard to miss.  Just look for the Cancun sign and the long line of people waiting to get that iconic selfie.  This beach is also called “El Mirador,” the lookout point.  There is a large wooden deck to the right of the Cancun sign where you can grab a great photo of the beach.  There are public bathrooms, public parking, free palapas, and lots of beach area to spread out if beach games are your style.  In case you want to check out a Mayan Ruin, El Rey is located just across the street.-CancunGuy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I recently visited this beach and it was beautiful the beach was very clean the sand was nice and white.No seaweed at least not when i went.They have vendors around the area that sell soda and water and little snacks and they also have a Cancun post where you can take photos with your own camera very nice place to visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its beautiful but it has no structure for staying. There is a long line to take in the lettters with the name Cancun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best Cancun beach to swim but the official Cancun landmak
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although Playa Delfines is not the best Cancun beach to swim (the ocean in this area has restless waters)  this is the official Cancun landmak, that colourful Cancun signal. Be prepared to stay in line to have a picture :-)At noon the ocean will reach its most beautiful color, a magnificent blue, you want be disappointed.As the most famous public beach in Cancun you will find some infrastructure at the place, like showers, restrooms and even parking.Enjoy it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: perfect beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we went on a Sunday and it wasn't too crowded. I would recommend brining snacks and drinks. The water was perfect.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best public beach in Cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I've been to other cities in Mexico and their public beaches are not as good as the one here in Cancun. It's easy to get here with bus, and there's this beautiful Cancun sign which you can take picture of/with (if you wait in line cause many people want to take pictures there). Also the beach is clean!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous Cancun sign
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful public white sandy beach on Boulevard Kukulkan. There are thatched umbrellas. This is a great place to have your picture taken with the famous Cancun sign. There is a line up of tourists to have their pictures taken during the day.  We asked our taxi driver to stop there on our way to our hotel to have our picture taken. It was 6 am. and there was no line up at that time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Come and take a picture on the CANCUN sign
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In playa delfines you can find the famous "CANCUN" big letters sign. Expect some waiting in line, as this is an obligated place for a picture with friends and family.If you decide to stay and enjoy the sun, make sure you stop by OXXO or Chedraui before, buy a foam cooler, a bag of ice and pack it with what you like for a time in the sun (soda, juice, water, etc), also some snacks. Many people offer food and beverages at the beach, but is usually overpriced and service is poor (specially if they detect you are not mexican).If you are a photography afficionado, from 7-9 AM or after 530 PM this becomes a great spot for pictures at the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and calm public beach in the hotel area! The CANCUN sign is just right there and it's a must visit for tourists! Get ready for long lines of travelers taking pictures there, but the beach itself is fantastic!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach right on the Atlantic/ Gulf of Mexico, warm waters. Great views, no large waves. Will return again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We Will Be BACK
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best scuba diving trip this year.  The beach is amazing for those who stayed behind. The atmosphere is exactly what you are looking for in a Caribbean get away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worlds best kept secret
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must visit spot if you’re in Cancun. Take the bus rather than the expensive taxis... the bus was only $12 (pesos). From the street, there’s not much to see but once you walk closer to the sidewalk and see that white sand, torquise water, and sun kissed bodies... your breath will be taken away. This side of the beach is actually pretty calm and was far less crowded than the spots closer to the shopping areas. The legendary CANCUN sign is at this beach as well. No matter the time of the day, expect to see a line for pictures in front of the sign. Don’t fret, just get in line and patiently wait for your turn, it’s worth it. I say this is the worlds best kept secret because most of the tourists skip this beach because there’s nothing around in this part of the strip... it’s perfect for your first or last day in Cancun just to spend the day taking in the beautiful scene.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of my favourite beaches in Mexico. It’s picturesque, beautiful, no photoshop needed :) and it’s not too crowded either, so you can have your own space. There were also waves, that we loved. Many places have rocks to break huge waves (because of accidents) but here you could swim in the sea, it’s not that dangerous. Absolutely loved it and would recommend it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is located on the southern end of the hotel zone. White sand, gentle wave,  great place to relax. You can take R-2 or R-1 bus to get here. I would not suggest walking.  It will take you a long time. Please know that the one side of the beach is the ocean and the other side are the back of resorts and hotels. If you were to walk along the beach , you may find yourself getting 'stuck' (no exit to main road) since the resorts often have guards to make sure no one enter the resort ( even just to cross lobby).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was one of our favorite beaches to play in waves with our 9 year old granddaughter.  More waves than some beaches but not too big of waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach. It was really beautiful and clean...volleyball net and nice comfy chairs to lay out in.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picturesque
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful white sandy beach free to the public has public bathrooms and the iconic Cancun colorful sign to take a family photo in front

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cancun sign was awesome thing to see. Beach is nice and clean with torquiose water. Highly recommended for everyoneIt gets busier at daytime with long lineups at cancun sign so we went early morning and there was only few people for photography.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best views in Cancun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want to experience the majesty of the Caribbean, you have to visit Delfines, you will have the best possible views in the Cancun area. Beach is clean most of the time and have enough space for your tent and beach chairs. Sea is not as calm as it may be farther south (Tulum), but for sure your family will enjoy their time dancing with the waves and having a sunbath.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointing
